title: Free Christian Baptist Church, torn down 1974
description: The Free (Christian) Baptist Church was organized in 1843 by Rev. G. W. Orser. Construction of the church began in 1871 using 10 x 10 timbers and no nails, but work stopped due to a doctrinal split. Rev. Charles McMullin continued the congregation with just 2 of the original 38 members, and the church was finally dedicated in 1875. Another split occurred in 1905, after which the congregation joined the Calvinist Church, forming the United Baptist Church. The building was later sold to Scott Sipprelle, who converted it into a garage with living quarters upstairs. It subsequently served as a blacksmith shop and was later sold to house the Hartland Furniture Company. This historic building, the oldest church in the area, was demolished in 1974.
